# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ -  All of the precious metals lost ground in price terms over the end of March and the start of April regardless of their underlying fundamentals. Two issues dominated: comments from the FOMC’s most recent meeting seemingly reduce the likelihood of a further round of US quantitative easing taking place. The Dollar rallied and a range of assets were sold off. On the following day, a disappointing Spanish bond auction drove a further sell-off of so-called “riskier” assets.  Leading up to the 3rd of April, futures investment activity was mixed across the precious metals. Gold and palladium saw speculative positioning fall whilst silver saw a rebound in long investor interest. Platinum positioning changed little. However, since that date, we expect the sharp price falls to have driven long liquidation and further dented confidence in the short term bullish prospects for the prices of these metals.  Net ETF flows were relatively light in the first week of April with none of the metals seeing determined moves by investors. Gold and palladium recorded net inflows while platinum and silver saw light selling instead. Also of note is that rhodium ETF holdings have risen by 10,650 ounces so far this year to a total of 27,200 ounces. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **10 April 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **10 April 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 3 April 2012; ETF data to 6 April 2012.** **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Gold moved in a range from $1,660 to $1,680 for the final few days of Q1 2012, climbing to a high of $1,683 on the 2nd of April. Macroeconomic news was then the spur for sharp downwards price movements on the 3rd and 4th. Late on the 3rd, the FOMC released the minutes from its most recent meeting. This demonstrated a lack of appetite for further quantitative easing which drove a reduction in risk appetite and a firmer US Dollar. Gold crashed down to $1,640 but was further pummelled the following day when an auction of Spanish bonds was less successful than hoped, sending gold down to a new low of $1,613 on the 4th. The price has since recovered some of its lost ground in climbing to $1,645 but the negative response to European economic concerns is a little worrying for gold bulls. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Apr12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

-  Net long speculative COMEX positions declined by 1.07 million ounces to 18.7 million ounces in the week to the 3rd of April. Open interest fell as a touch of long liquidation was seen. Given the sharp downwards movement in the price since the 3rd, we expect the next commitment of traders report to show more long liquidation. We would not be surprised to see short interest starting to grow as the gold price fails to make positive headway. TOCOM positions continued to climb from their late February low of 925,000 ounces, adding another 220,000 ounces and rising to 1.38 million ounces. -  After net selling of roughly half a tonne of gold by ETF investors in the last week of March, ETF holdings increased by roughly a tonne of gold in the first week of April. There is, though, no real momentum in this market currently, either positive or negative, with total global holdings having been between 70 and 71 million ounces since the start of February. 2 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **10 April 2012** ### **Silver CFTC data to 3 April 2012; ETF data to 6 April 2012.</

-  Silver showed little independence from gold over the end of the first quarter of the year. With the gold:silver ratio almost unchanged, currency movements and fluctuations in risk appetite drove silver prices as well as gold. Silver found some support at $32 towards the end of March and raced to a high of $33.15 on the 2nd of April. However, comments from the FOMC depressed many commodity prices on the 3rd. Silver fared less badly than did gold , falling back only to $32.50 but it slid down to close to $31 on the following day as a poor Spanish bond auction drove selling of a range of “risk” assets. Silver’s recovery since then has been less than convincing, with the price now just above $31.60. -  After four successive weeks of declines, net long speculative COMEX silver interest finally rebounded in the week to the 3rd of April, rising by 8.9 million ounces to 178 million ounces. Although this is much higher than the low levels of positioning seen at the start of the year, it does not make an entirely credible bullish case. Open interest increased and investors opened fresh long positions but additional short interest was seen too. Recent price movements may have driven even more short interest in this volatile metal. -  As with gold, silver ETF positions have been relatively static in recent weeks

. In the first week of April, many of the funds we monitor saw net inflows of silver but this was outweighed by selling in the ETF Securities funds and from the larger iShares fund. Holdings fell by 1.94 million ounces during the week to 458 million ounces. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **10 April 2012** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 3 April 2012; ETF data to 6 April 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |||_Futures_

-  Like silver, platinum showed little independence from gold in price terms over the end of the first quarter of 2012. Where gold struggled, platinum struggled too as investors treated the two metals identically, regardless of fundamentals or news flow. Gold maintained its unaccustomed premium to platinum at roughly $30 an ounce. Macroeconomic news dominated as platinum slid lower after the exuberance of January and February. Platinum did climb from a low of $1,625 on the 29th of March to a high of $1,668 on the 3rd before the receding chances of further US quantitative easing and the recurring worries over European sovereign debt weighed on the precious metal sector. Platinum crashed to $1,640 on the 3rd of April and a short-lived low of $1,590 on the 5th, bringing out price-sensitive Chinese buying to provide some support. Platinum has since rallied to $1,610 but confidence is fragile. -  After four successive weekly falls, net long speculative interest in platinum on NYMEX finally climbed in the week to the

3rd of April. However, it rose only by 7,500 ounces in reaching 1.62 million ounces. Despite a series of news stories focusing on supply side disruptions in the platinum market, investors remain unconvinced and downwards pressure from risk-off trades has weighed on platinum. However, short positioning shrank, a positive sign of improving sentiment given that this was not driven by price moves. TOCOM interest continues to rebound from its February lows to provide a little support for the price. -  After gentle buying interest had been seen in the final week of the first quarter of 2012, optimists for the platinum price will have been disappointed by net selling of 3,900 ounces of platinum from ETF vaults. However, all of this selling came from the US funds and we do not feel that it represents a change of opinion towards a more bearish outlook. Holdings stand at 1.49 million ounces. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **10 April 2012** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 3 April 2012; ETF data to 6 April 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

-  The palladium price continued to languish under $700 throughout the end of March and the start of April, although it remained well above its early January lows for the year-to-date. More positively, the decline in the price which had been taking place since mid-March slowed as palladium approached $630. A degree of selling as the end of the first quarter of the year approached was

not too surprising, particularly given concerns over a slowing Chinese economy which is seen as vital for industrial commodity demand. Palladium slipped from $670 on the 27th of March to a low of $640 on the 29th before bouncing to a new high of $665 on the 2nd. Unexpectedly positive comments from the US Federal Reserve strengthened the Dollar and dampened hopes of further quantitative easing, weighing on many asset prices. Palladium slipped to a new low of $630 on the 5th of April before bouncing to its current $647 with the market becoming ever more bearish. 

-  Having been unable to push palladium far above $700, investor interest in this metal has declined dramatically, falling from 1.24 million ounces of net speculative long positions on NYMEX in early March to 726,000 ounces now after a weekly decline of 200,000 ounces. Long interest fell and short positioning increased. We feel that there is scope for short covering to help the price move higher at some point but sentiment remains rather depressed currently. 

-  Low palladium prices finally seem to have provided a buying opportunity for ETF investors who added 8,700 ounces to their positions in the first week of April after net buying of 15,600 ounces a week before (recalculated from last week’s report using new ETF data). Metal holdings now sit at a global 2.00 million ounces after 280,000 ounces of net buying in Q1 2012. This is the first time that positions have been above the two million ounce level since September 2011.
